Every reported statistic reproduces to the digit: RT = 0.592485; mean |discrepancy| = 4.7350 kcal/mol (reviewer: 4.73); range 3.8512-5.7253 (reviewer: 3.85-5.73); mean 3.4708 log10 units (reviewer: 3.47); range 2.8229-4.1967 (reviewer: 2.82-4.20); pairs consistent within 0.5 kcal/mol = 0/25. Worked examples check out exactly: line 146, -18.4 kcal/mol -> Kd = 3.256e-14 M (32.6 fM), 0.32 nM -> -12.95 kcal/mol, gap 5.45 / 3.99 decades; line 290, -19.5 -> 5.086e-15 M, 0.08 nM -> -13.77, gap 5.73 / 4.20 (worst); line 384 mildest at 3.85 / 2.82. My OLS of stated on thermodynamically-correct dG gives slope 1.77129, intercept 4.68170, R2 = 0.993908, max residual 0.2204 -- identical to the reviewer's 1.771 / 4.682 / 0.9939 / 0.22. Regressing stated dG on ln(Kd) gives 1.04946 kcal/mol per ln unit, implying T = 528.11 K. Also verified the rendering path: app.js:562-563 splits the string on '|' into two independently-displayed badges, and app.js:636 prints the whole string, so the two contradictory numbers are presented side by side as corroborating measurements. Verified the absence of any temperature or standard-state statement: grep for 298/kelvin/standard state/uncertain across the three content files returns only 'Asp298'/'Glu319' residue hits. Nothing in this finding is overstated. Correction: None to the analysis. One framing addition: the reviewer's affine-rescaling result (gain 1.77, R2 0.994) is strong evidence that ONE column was written first and the other mechanically transformed, but it does not by itself identify which. The Kd column is the more likely primary (its values are round to 1-2 significant figures: 0.08, 0.14, 0.18, 0.22, 0.32, 0.35, 0.52, 0.65, 0.85, 1.2, ... 4.8 nM), which is worth stating because it determines what the remediation should keep.

(1) 'B' is NOT 'not a standard one-letter amino acid code' -- B is the IUPAC/IUB one-letter code for Asx (Asn-or-Asp ambiguity). The reviewer's conclusion is right but the premise as written is wrong and a domain reader will catch it. Correct wording: B is an ambiguity code, not one of the 20 canonical residues; it has no defined side chain, so it cannot be assigned coordinates or force-field parameters, and the AlphaFold Server rejects it -- which independently proves no AF3 run was performed on app.js:173, 371 or 130. (2) The reviewer under-reports the evidence. The same-input contradiction extends to the hardcoded pLDDT, which is the single quantity AlphaFold3 actually emits and therefore the cleanest falsification available: the identical 36-mer carries pLDDT 94.8 (app.js:156), 94.3 (app.js:250) and 92.8 (app.js:134); the identical 41-mer carries 93.2 (app.js:198), 92.8 (app.js:322) and 90.7 (app.js:134). I also find 14 of the 35 distinct sequences carry an ODD number of cysteines (up to 9, e.g. app.js:125 and 128) with disulfide connectivity never specified -- a further input-underdetermination the reviewer's proposed canonical-code validator would not catch.

text: Verdict PARTIALLY_REFUTED on CT-03: The arithmetic converting dG to Kd is exact (-18.2 -> 45.6 fM, -18.4 -> 32.6, -18.7 -> 19.6, -18.9 -> 14.0, -19.1 -> 10.0, -19.5 -> 5.09 fM; the remaining values span -15.2 -> 7.2 pM to -17.8 -> 90 fM; LE = 19.5/295 = 0.066). But the finding's headline -- an 'empirical ceiling for non-covalent binding' at ~-18 kcal/mol that 6 of 25 candidates 'exceed' -- does not survive three independent checks. (a) THE COUNT IS WRONG. At the reviewer's own calibration Kd = 4e-14 M -> dG = -18.28, only FIVE candidates are more negative (-18.4, -18.7, -18.9, -19.1, -19.5). The reviewer lists app.js:394 (-18.2) among the six, but -18.2 > -18.28, so it does not exceed. (b) THE CITED SOURCE SAYS SOMETHING ELSE. I retrieved Delgadillo et al., PLoS ONE 2019;14(2):e0204194 (PMID 30818336, doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0204194) -- the paper the reviewer cites for the biotin calibration. Its abstract states 'The high affinity (KD ~ 10-15 M) of biotin for avidin and streptavidin'. At KD = 1e-15 M, dG = -20.46 kcal/mol and ZERO of the 25 candidates exceed it. The 4e-14 figure is defensible from Kuntz's Table 1 (I confirmed it lists biotin-streptavidin at -log K1 = 13.43, i.e. Kd = 3.7e-14 -> dG = -18.32) but it is not what the cited paper reports, and the reviewer selected the loosest value in a range that spans 1e-15 to 4e-14, which maximizes the count. (c) THE PHYSICS FRAMING IS DOMAIN OVERREACH. I retrieved Kuntz et al., PNAS 1999;96(18):9997-10002 (PMID 10468550, doi 10.1073/pnas.96.18.9997) and the full text: the plateau it reports is '~-15 kcal/mol (i.e., picomolar dissociation constants)', NOT '-18 kcal/mol' as the reviewer's ground_truth states, and the analysis is per-non-hydrogen-atom for SMALL-MOLECULE ligands -- it does not define a ceiling for protein/peptide interfaces. There is no such ceiling: barnase-barstar, a natural non-covalent protein-protein complex, has Kd ~ 1.3e-14 M and dG0 ~ -19 kcal/mol, essentially equal to the platform's most extreme claim. So '-19.5 kcal/mol is beyond the empirical ceiling for non-covalent binding' is false as stated. What IS true and survives is the modality argument: Cao et al., Nature 2022;605:551-560 (PMID 35332283, doi 10.1038/s41586-022-04654-9) -- abstract verified -- reports binders 'smaller than 65 amino acids' that are 'hyperstable' and reach 'nanomolar to picomolar affinities' only 'following experimental optimization'. The platform claims 5-45 fM to 7 pM, uniformly, for unoptimized flexible LINEAR 26-47-mers with unspecified disulfides, across six unrelated target classes, with no experimental data. That is the real finding. Correction: Rewrite the finding as an achievability argument, not a ceiling argument. Correct text: 'The stated dG magnitudes are 3-6 kcal/mol outside the range achievable by de novo peptide design. Cao et al. (Nature 2022) reach nanomolar-to-picomolar only after experimental affinity maturation, and only for hyperstable folded mini-proteins; these candidates are unoptimized flexible linear peptides with GGGGS linkers and unpaired cysteines, for which a large conformational-entropy penalty applies. Kuntz et al. (PNAS 1999) place the plateau for tight ligands at ~-15 kcal/mol; 25 of 25 candidates exceed that plateau and 5 approach barnase-barstar (dG0 ~ -19 kcal/mol), the tightest natural protein-protein complex known.' DELETE the sentence 'Six of the 25 candidates are therefore claimed to bind more tightly than biotin-streptavidin' and delete the Delgadillo citation from this finding's ground_truth, or re-cite it accurately as reporting KD ~ 1e-15 M. Keep the Cao and Kuntz citations, which I verified.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on CT-04: I ran the reviewer's grep myself over README.md, app.js, index.html and styles.css with the full alternation (vina|smina|gnina|autodock|rosetta|openmm|gromacs|amber|namd|mmgbsa|mm-gbsa|mmpbsa|prodigy|boltz|diffdock|foldx|glide|alchemical|thermodynam|Math.log|Math.exp|boltzmann). It returns exactly one line: README.md:108, matching only on 'Amber' used as a UI colour name. The absence claim is exact. `git ls-files` gives 235 tracked paths; the only non-.agents entries are .gitignore, README.md, app.js, index.html, skills-lock.json, styles.css (the reviewer omitted .gitignore, immaterial). No .pdb/.cif/.mmcif/AF3 confidence JSON is tracked. I also checked the untracked directories the reviewer did not see (data/, research/, mas/, memory/, platform/, reviews/, .venv/, all dated 2026-08-16, twelve days after the platform commits): data/extracted_raw.json is a JSON re-dump of NATURAL_PRODUCTS_DATA and the same hardcoded records, not AF3 output, so the absence claim holds against the full working tree, not just the index. I verified every cited generator verbatim -- app.js:707 comment, app.js:715 `radius = 6 + (charCode % 5) * 0.8`, app.js:791 `score = 93 + Math.sin(i * 0.4) * 4 + (char.charCodeAt(0) % 5) * 0.5`, app.js:850 `error = Math.abs(i - j) * 0.4 + (...charCodeAt(i % len) % 4) * 0.3`, app.js:905, app.js:1071. I grepped for fetch(/XMLHttpRequest/axios across app.js and index.html: zero hits; alphafoldserver.com appears only as two `<a href>` at index.html:42 and 363, so 'AlphaFold Server Live Connected' is a hyperlink and no prediction is ever requested or retrieved. On the capability claim itself, the AF3 paper (Abramson et al., Nature 2024;630:493-500, PMID 38718835, doi 10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w) describes structure prediction of complexes with no affinity output, and I found independent third-party confirmation in the reviewer's own Boltz-2 citation (PMID 40667369, doi 10.1101/2025.06.14.659707), whose abstract states directly that 'recent advances, such as AlphaFold3 and Boltz-1 ... still fall short in predicting binding affinity'. This is the strongest and best-supported finding in the review. Correction: The finding is correct as written. One correction to the REMEDIATION, not the finding (see fix_is_sound): the fix recommends PRODIGY as 'the correct tool class for this project's actual modality'. PRODIGY's contacts model was fitted and validated on a benchmark of folded protein-protein complexes (I verified R = -0.73, RMSE = 1.89 kcal/mol on the 81-complex reliable subset in Vangone & Bonvin, eLife 2015;4:e07454, PMID 26193119). Short flexible linear peptides fall outside that applicability domain, and -- decisively -- PRODIGY cannot see the covalently attached natural-product warhead at all, so it would score the wrong chemical entity for all 25 records.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on CT-05: The absence claims are exact: I grepped all three content files for plus-minus signs, '+/-', 298, kelvin, 'standard state', 'error bar', 'uncertaint', 's.e.m', 'stderr' -- the only hits are 'Asp298'/'Glu319' residue labels. No method, version, temperature, standard state, replicate count, or interval appears anywhere. The cited leaderboard gaps are correct: rank 4 (-14.2, app.js:128) vs rank 5 (-14.8, app.js:129) = 0.6 kcal/mol; rank 7 (-12.6, app.js:131) vs rank 8 (-13.0, app.js:132) = 0.4. The core argument -- that one-decimal point estimates with no interval read as measurements and license comparisons the data cannot support -- is correct, is squarely within the discipline, and I independently confirm the PRODIGY error bar (RMSE 1.89 kcal/mol) that anchors it. The CASF-2016 characterization (scoring power weakest of the four metrics; docking scores useful for enrichment, not kcal/mol) and the Genheden & Ryde positioning of MM-GB/PBSA as intermediate and requiring per-system calibration are both standard and correctly stated. Correction: Two corrections. (1) The sentence 'The dG differences that drive the entire leaderboard ordering' is factually wrong and contradicts the reviewer's own CT-06. dG does NOT drive the ordering -- it inverts three times (ranks 4/5, 7/8, 9/10; r(dG, rank) = +0.949, not 1.0). The correct and stronger statement is that the dG column is displayed adjacent to the rank column as though it justified the ordering while in fact reproducing none of it. (2) The ground_truth asserts 'ABFE RMSE historically 0.8-2.3 kcal/mol, ~1.1 achievable after zero-point shifting' and 'experimental reproducibility between independent assays is itself ~0.9 kcal/mol and can reach 2 kcal/mol'. These are plausible and consistent with the published assay-reproducibility literature (independent IC50 replicates in curated databases scatter by roughly 0.7 log units, ~0.9 kcal/mol), but the reviewer supplies NO citation for either number in a review whose central charge is unsourced numbers. Either cite them or soften to 'of order 1-2 kcal/mol'. Also add, as the practical consequence of the fix: with a 1.9 kcal/mol error bar and a 6.1 kcal/mol total spread, the ten candidates collapse to roughly three indistinguishable bands -- so 'suppress orderings whose gaps fall inside the stated error' means deleting the 1-10 leaderboard, and the report should say so rather than leave it as an exercise.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on CT-06: The substance is correct and I confirm every structural claim: CEI is a hardcoded literal at app.js:125-134 with no formula, inputs, units, weights, validation set or reference anywhere in the repository; it is rendered as a gold-badged leaderboard column (app.js:886, index.html:306) under the heading 'TOP 10 Candidate Computational Benchmark' (index.html:316); and the chart at app.js:1057-1078 puts CEI (dimensionless, 0-100) and |dG| (kcal/mol) in two bar datasets with no `yAxisID` on either -- I grepped, there are zero occurrences of yAxisID in app.js -- so Chart.js renders both against a single shared y-axis, exactly as described. I reproduce the reviewer's correlations to the digit: r(CEI, rank) = -0.9845, r(CEI, dG) = -0.9389, r(pLDDT, dG) = -0.3798. The point that no in silico pipeline outputs a cognition score, and that a benchmark column nobody can reproduce is unfalsifiable, is correct and well within discipline. Correction: One factual error to fix before issue. The claim 'They are strictly monotone with the assigned rank' is FALSE: the CEI series is 98.4, 95.2, 92.1, 93.8, 90.5, 89.0, 87.6, 85.4, 83.9, 82.5 -- rank 3 (92.1) is LOWER than rank 4 (93.8). A correlation of -0.985 is not strict monotonicity, and the inference the reviewer draws from it ('this shows the leaderboard is ordered by CEI, i.e. by the undefined quantity') is therefore unsupported. Replace it with the stronger and verifiable statement: the rank column is an independent hardcoded literal that NO displayed metric reproduces -- CEI has 1 inversion, dG has 3, pLDDT has 4 -- so the 'TOP 10' ordering is not a ranking by anything present in the table, and CEI is merely its closest correlate. Also broaden the scope: CEI is not the only undefined index. The same defect appears 21 times as 'Seizure Index' (app.js:147-395 and README.md:100), plus 'Safety Plasticity Score: 99.5 / 100' (app.js:291), 'Safety Index: 99.1 / 100' and '99.3 / 100' (app.js:343, 395), 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' (app.js:281), 'Cytokine Storm Risk: 0%' (app.js:323) and 'Tolerance Rate: 0.0%' (app.js:157) -- undefined composites reported as probabilities of exactly zero or one, a stronger claim than CEI ever makes. Any remediation that deletes only `cei` leaves the larger instance of the same defect in place.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: NO CHEMICAL DEFINITION OF ANY MOLECULE EXISTS -- a more fundamental blocker than CT-02. Every candidate is a bio-conjugate of a natural-product warhead plus a peptide, but the warhead is given only as prose plus a molecular formula ('Ginsenoside Rg1 Dammarane-12,20-diol (C42H72O14) + C-20 Linker', app.js:142; 'Huperzine A Pyridone Core (C15H18N2O) + Cys-Lys Amide Coupling', app.js:152; 'Onjisaponin V Presenegenin Aglycone (C30H46O6) + 1,2,3-Triazole Linker', app.js:182) and the `sequence` field carries only the peptide half. No SMILES, no CCD code, no attachment atom, no linker topology, no stereocentres, no protonation state, no disulfide connectivity. Even a reviewer who accepted the intent could not compute these numbers: 25 of 25 records are chemically underdetermined. Note also that a full SMILES exists for the free natural products at app.js:10-80 -- so the omission is specifically at the conjugate, the thing whose dG is claimed. (Two of those SMILES are also invalid: app.js:50 curcumin contains the literal token 'OCH3', which is not valid SMILES; app.js:60 and 70 contain molecular formulas, not SMILES.)

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: A BISPECIFIC OR TRI-FUNCTIONAL CONJUGATE CANNOT HAVE A SINGLE dG OR Kd -- an unflagged thermodynamic category error, and the mechanism by which the most extreme values are generated. app.js:238 reports one dG/Kd for a molecule binding both alpha7 nAChR ECD and GluN2A NTD; app.js:290 reports one for AChE plus TrkA plus M1 mAChR; app.js:342 for Trem2 plus Keap1; app.js:394 for ER-beta plus EAAT2. These are separate equilibria with separate constants. A single number exists only for a defined ternary complex and only with an explicit effective-concentration/avidity term, which is never stated. Note the four 'Dual/Super/Bispecific' entries hold four of the five most negative values in the dataset -- the marketing tier is doing the thermodynamics.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE IMPLIED KINETICS ARE ABSURD AND ARE NEVER STATED. No kon, koff or residence time appears anywhere in the repository. At the flagship Kd = 5.09 fM (app.js:290) and a realistic peptide association rate of 1e5-1e7 M-1 s-1, koff = 5.1e-10 to 5.1e-8 s-1, i.e. a dissociation half-life of 0.4 to 43 years. This is quantitatively irreconcilable with README.md:102 ('Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days'), with README.md:100 ('Allosteric NMDAR tuners feature capped Emax'), and with app.js:15's own description of huperzine A as a 'potent REVERSIBLE acetylcholinesterase inhibitor'. CT-03 gestures at 'effectively irreversible' but never computes it; the computed half-life is the single most legible way to show a non-specialist that the number is impossible.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: README.md AND app.js DISAGREE ABOUT WHICH MOLECULE EACH dG BELONGS TO -- an independent, cross-file proof of fabrication that the review does not use. README.md:60 assigns HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 the peptide CVDRENPVEWVRAC (14 residues) with dG = -18.4; app.js:143 assigns the same drug a 47-residue sequence with the identical dG = -18.4. README.md:61 gives X2 the 8-mer KWWKFLRR at -16.2 while app.js:153 gives a 36-mer at -16.2. README.md:62 gives X3 the 12-mer DEETGEFLFQLP at -15.8 while app.js:163 gives a 28-mer at -15.8. The reported free energy is invariant to a three-fold change in the length of the molecule. No estimator -- physical or learned -- is invariant to that. This is cleaner evidence than the duplicate-sequence argument because it requires no assumption about what was run.

KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG (app.js:153 and 247, the highest-valued AChE binder) is a 36-mer with 13 Lys/Arg and 4 Glu/Asp -- net charge +9, 36% cationic, 4 Trp -- the canonical cationic-amphipathic profile of a membrane-lytic / cell-penetrating peptide, not of a CNS therapeutic. This directly contradicts README.md:99, which claims 'hydrophobic peptide linkers sterically prevent binding to hERG pore Tyr652/Phe656': highly charged amphipathic peptides are associated with nonspecific membrane and channel perturbation, not protection from it, and a peptide of this class would not be assayed against hERG in the first place because the stated 'IC50 > 50 uM' is a small-molecule endpoint applied to the wrong modality. Separately, 14 of the 35 distinct sequences carry an ODD number of cysteines (up to 9, at app.js:125 and 128) with disulfide pairing never specified -- both a missing required input for any structure or energy calculation and a first-order determinant of the conformational-entropy penalty CT-03 invokes.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE PAE PANEL IS WRONG ON ITS OWN TERMS, BEYOND BEING SYNTHETIC. app.js:844 caps the matrix at gridSize = min(length, 45), so any candidate longer than 45 residues is silently truncated (the 100-residue rank-1 candidate at app.js:125 would display 45% of itself with no indication). The maximum value the generator can reach at gridSize 45 is 45*0.4 + 0.9 = 18.9 A, so the axis label '0 - 30 A' at index.html:397 is unreachable by construction. And the alpha ramp at app.js:862, `1 - error/35`, renders HIGH predicted error as nearly transparent, i.e. the lowest-confidence regions read as background -- the inverse of the AF3 convention, where high PAE is the visually dominant off-diagonal block. A reader comparing this panel to a real AF3 output is being shown a reversed colour semantic.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: NO CONTROLS, NO RETROSPECTIVE VALIDATION, NO APPLICABILITY DOMAIN. A credible affinity layer is judged on controls before it is judged on predictions: redock a solved complex and report RMSD, score a known binder against a known non-binder on the same target, report enrichment on a decoy set. Nothing here scores a single reference ligand -- huperzine A against AChE is the obvious positive control with experimental Ki/IC50 available in ChEMBL, and the repository already contains its SMILES at app.js:10. Without one scored control there is no evidence the pipeline could rank even a case whose answer is known, which is the precondition for any of the reviewer's proposed remediation tiers to be worth adding.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE AChE BINDING-SITE RESIDUE LISTS MIX TWO INCOMPATIBLE NUMBERING CONVENTIONS -- and the review's overall_assessment explicitly praises them as 'correct textbook structural pharmacology', which overstates. app.js:154 lists 'AChE CAS (Trp84, Phe330, Tyr121) & PAS (Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr341)' and app.js:248 lists 'Trp84, Phe330, Trp286, Tyr341': Trp84/Phe330/Tyr121 are Torpedo californica numbering, while Trp286/Tyr72/Tyr341 are human AChE numbering (the Torpedo equivalents are Trp279/Tyr70/Tyr334; the human equivalents of Trp84/Phe330 are Trp86/Phe338). app.js:12 uses Trp279 for the PAS while app.js:154 uses Trp286 for the same site. This matters directly to this discipline because these residue lists are precisely the input to the per-residue decomposition the review proposes under the gmx_MMPBSA remediation -- a decomposition keyed to a mixed-species numbering scheme cannot be mapped onto any prepared receptor.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE PROPOSED FIXES ARE NOT SAFE TO IMPLEMENT IN THE ORDER GIVEN. CT-01's remediation -- store kd_M, compute dg = RT*ln(kd_M) at render time, add a unit test asserting |dG - RT ln Kd| < 0.01 -- is arithmetically correct (I verified RT = 0.0019872041*298.15 = 0.592485 and the sign convention) but if implemented ALONE it makes 25 fabricated numbers thermodynamically self-consistent, removing the single most legible external signal that the dataset is invented and making the platform strictly more convincing to a non-specialist. It must be gated behind CT-02's remediation (remove the values or mark them 'not computed'), and the report should say so explicitly, because a downstream implementer reading these findings in order will do CT-01 first since it is the smallest patch. The unit test as specified is also either vacuous (if only kd_M is persisted there is no second value to compare) or brittle (a 0.01 kcal/mol tolerance is tighter than the 0.1 kcal/mol display rounding); it should assert over any persisted pair with a tolerance derived from the display precision.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: NO TIER IN THE PROPOSED REMEDIATION ACTUALLY PRODUCES A NUMBER FOR THIS MODALITY, AND THE REVIEW DOES NOT SAY SO PLAINLY. CT-04's fix lists Vina/gnina (small molecules, poses not kcal/mol), gmx_MMPBSA (relative ranking within a congeneric series), PRODIGY (folded protein-protein complexes, cannot see the covalent warhead), Boltz-2 (small-molecule potency), and ABFE (which the reviewer concedes 'for 30-50-mer flexible peptides is not a solved problem'). Every entry is either the wrong chemistry or the wrong modality for a peptide-small-molecule bio-conjugate binding a receptor ectodomain. The honest conclusion the review stops one step short of: for this modality there is currently no computational method that legitimately returns a kcal/mol, so the correct remediation is to display no affinity at all until experimental SPR/ITC data exist -- not to substitute a differently-labelled prediction with an error bar.

task: propagate the CT-03 ceiling refutation to its calibration-point claim

rationale: The Application half of this record is withdrawn; the citation is not. This claim supplied the CEILING calibration point for CT-03 -- Kd ~4e-14 M, dG -18.3 kcal/mol -- and used it to read dG -19.5 (app.js:290) as ~8x tighter than the tightest non-covalent complex known, i.e. as a physical impossibility rather than a design-plausibility problem. The same verification that refuted clm_bbdc9a4a843be19b (sts_1e15e64230f347b8, PARTIALLY_REFUTED, 2026-08-17) refuted that reading on three counts: the cited source reports K_D ~1e-15 M for biotin-avidin, i.e. dG -20.46, at which ZERO of the 25 candidates exceed it, and -18.3 is the loosest end of a range spanning 1e-15 to 4e-14; Kuntz et al., PNAS 1999;96:9997 place the plateau at ~-15 kcal/mol and define it per non-hydrogen atom for SMALL MOLECULES, not for peptide interfaces; and barnase-barstar, a natural non-covalent protein-protein complex, sits at dG0 ~ -19 kcal/mol, essentially equal to the most extreme value the gate rejects. Filed as retractions.jsonl#ret_0004. WHAT SURVIVES: the achievability argument -- the stated magnitudes are 3-6 kcal/mol outside the range de novo peptide design reaches (Cao et al., Nature 2022;605:551 reach nanomolar to picomolar only after experimental affinity maturation, and only for hyperstable folded mini-proteins). The cited paper and its characterisation of the biotin-streptavidin interaction are not in question; what is withdrawn is its use here as a ceiling. This record propagates the 2026-08-17 verification to the sibling literature claim the refuted finding was derived from: platform/check_retractions.py found the ceiling reading still standing on memory/views/claims.md, three files from the refutation that killed it.
